sentences.text: Applicant/complainant thereafter filed a revision petition challenging the above order mainly on ground that statements under Sections 200 and 202 Cr.P.C. were not considered, wherein there was a specific allegation of criminal breach of trust that despite money was paid towards an unregistered agreement of sale, by online transaction but dishonestly it was not executed by proposed accused persons.

entities.text: Razi Ahmad vs State Of Up And 2 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Revisional Court by order dated 20.01.2024 has rejected the said revision petition and relevant part thereof is reproduced hereinafter :-

"10. This Revisional Court has perused the statement of complainant Razi Ahmad under Section 200 of the Code of Criminal and that of witnesses Zahiruddin Ahmad and Fariyad Ahmad under Section 202 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and perused the other record.
At this stage, only prima-facie case is to be seen in the light of evidence available on record.

From the perusal of statement of complainant Razi Ahmad under Section 200 of the Code of Criminal and that of witnesses Zahiruddin Ahmad and Fariyad Ahmad under Section 202 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and documents available on record, the learned Magistrate has found that prima-facie offence punishable under section 506 of the Indian Penal Code against the proposed accused persons is made out.
Thus, it transpires that after perusing and scrutinizing the entire records, the learned Magistrate has passed the impugned order after applying its judicial mind.
Civil suit is stated to be pending in between the parties.

11. In the backdrop of above discussion and the principles laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court and Hon'ble Allahabad High Court in above case laws, I find that Revisional Court has limited power in interfering with the order challenged U/s. 397 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
It can not be said that the impugned order is based on no material.
The impugned order is not perverse.
The learned Court below has not committed any illegality, impropriety, irregularity or jurisdictional error in passing the impugned order.
Therefore, this revision is liable to be dismissed."

Sri Amit Kumar Singh, learned counsel for applicant submits that above referred finding returned by Revisional Court that learned Magistrate has passed the impugned summoning order after careful perusal of statement recorded under Sections 200 and 202 Cr.P.C. are perverse, since the statements has not been recorded even in brief in impugned order.
Learned counsel refers statement of complainant as recorded under Section 200 Cr.P.C.

entities.text: Razi Ahmad vs State Of Up And 2 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: I have considered the above submissions and finds that there is merit in above arguments as learned Magistrate has not considered about the online transaction as well as no reason has been assigned in impugned order that why offences of criminal breach of trust is not made out and only offence under Section 506 I.P.C. is made out.

The Revisional Court has also not considered the specific grounds raised in memo of revision and as referred above a perverse finding is being recorded in regard to appreciation of statements recorded under Sections 200 and 202 Cr.P.C. by the concerned Magistrate.
In the aforesaid circumstances, impugned order dated 20.02.2024 passed in Criminal Revision No.57 of 2023 (Razi Ahmad Vs. State of U.P. and others) is set aside.

entities.text: Criminal Revision No.57 of 2023 (Razi Ahmad Vs. State of U.P. and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, considering that this order is passed without issuing notice to opposite party Nos.2 and 3 (accused), therefore, matter is remitted back to Revisional Court to pass fresh order after hearing the rival parties within three months.
Revisional Court will also take note of Lalankumar Singh and others Vs. State of Maharashtra, 2022 SCC OnLine SC 1383 as well as ingredients of Sections 406 and 420 I.P.C., as the case may be.

entities.text: Lalankumar Singh and others Vs. State of Maharashtra, 2022 SCC OnLine SC 1383
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, application is disposed of with aforesaid observation.

opennyai_summary.decision:
In the aforesaid circumstances, impugned order dated 20.02.2024 passed in Criminal Revision No.57 of 2023 (Razi Ahmad Vs. State of U.P. and others) is set aside.
However, considering that this order is passed without issuing notice to opposite party Nos.2 and 3 (accused), therefore, matter is remitted back to Revisional Court to pass fresh order after hearing the rival parties within three months.
Revisional Court will also take note of Lalankumar Singh and others Vs. State of Maharashtra, 2022 SCC OnLine SC 1383 as well as ingredients of Sections 406 and 420 I.P.C., as the case may be.
Accordingly, application is disposed of with aforesaid observation.
